claim: Deferring the SendGrid cancel to a 15-minute cron means any booking cancelled/rescheduled less than roughly 15-25 minutes before a reminder's send time still gets the reminder sent, because the next cron run is after sendAt and the row is then just deleted by the past-date cleanup.
body:
## [ISSUE] Cancellations made shortly before the send time never reach SendGrid

**Severity:** HIGH — reminder emails are still sent for bookings cancelled/rescheduled close to the reminder time, which is exactly the bug this PR is meant to fix.

### The Problem
Before this PR, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` sent `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends {status: "cancel"}` right away. Now the non-immediate path (`handleCancelBooking.ts:488`, `bookings.tsx:490` requestReschedule, `workflows.tsx:378/576`) only sets `cancelled: true`. The SendGrid cancel happens only here:

```ts
const remindersToCancel = await prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({
  where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour").toISOString() } },
});
```

This cron runs at minutes 0/15/30/45 (`.github/workflows/cron-scheduleEmailReminders.yml:8`).

### Theory / Proof
Say a reminder has `sendAt` = 10:20 and the booking is cancelled at 10:10:
1. The 10:00 run happens before the cancellation, so the row is not `cancelled` yet.
2. At 10:10 the row gets `cancelled: true` and nothing is sent to SendGrid.
3. At 10:20 SendGrid delivers the email.
4. At 10:30 the cleanup at line 34 (`deleteMany ... scheduledDate lte now`) deletes the row without anyone ever cancelling it.

SendGrid also needs the cancel to be registered some time before `send_at` (their docs say cancellations within about 10 minutes of the send time are not guaranteed). So the unprotected window is up to 15 minutes of cron period plus the lead time SendGrid needs.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Cancellations made more than about 25 minutes before the send time work. "Cancel 15 minutes before the meeting" is a common real case, and for BEFORE_EVENT reminders with short offsets it is the main case. Those regress compared to the pre-PR immediate cancel.

### Research
SendGrid Cancel Scheduled Sends docs: a cancelled batch stays in `scheduled_sends` until its send time, and the account can have at most 100 pending cancellations. That is why the author defers the cancel. The deferral only has to cover reminders that are far away. For reminders that are close, an immediate cancel only takes up a slot for a short time.

### Recommendation
If the reminder is already inside the cron's window, cancel it right away in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`. Only defer the ones further out:

```ts
if (immediateDelete || dayjs(scheduledDate).isBefore(dayjs().add(1, "hour"))) {
  await client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", method: "POST",
    body: { batch_id: referenceId, status: "cancel" } });
  await prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } });
  return;
}
await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminderId }, data: { cancelled: true } });
```
(pass `scheduledDate` from the callers, which already have the reminder row). Also make the cron's window cover at least cron period + SendGrid lead time (e.g. `add(1, "hour")` is fine as long as the immediate path covers < 1h).

claim: One try/catch wraps the whole cancel loop, so a single failing SendGrid request aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders in the run, and the lazily-built prisma.delete promises for already-cancelled batches are never executed.

Rescheduling via handleNewBooking (and workflow/step deletion) still uses immediateDelete=true, which issues SendGrid cancels immediately and so still consumes the 100 pending-cancellation quota the PR says caused the bug; failed cancels are only logged and the email is still sent.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] The reschedule path still cancels in SendGrid right away, so it still counts against the 100-cancellation limit

**Severity:** MEDIUM — the most common way reminders get cancelled (an attendee rescheduling) still runs into the failure mode this PR describes.

### The Problem
```ts
originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => {
  if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL) {
    deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true);
```
With `immediateDelete = true`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (`emailReminderManager.ts`) sends `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends {status:"cancel"}` right away and returns. The same flag is used for workflow deletion (`workflows.tsx:214`) and step deletion (`workflows.tsx:521`).

### Theory / Proof
The PR description gives the root cause of #7225: SendGrid keeps a cancelled batch in `scheduled_sends` until its send time, and an account can have at most 100 pending cancellations. Reminders are scheduled at SendGrid up to 72h ahead. So every immediate cancel takes up a slot for up to 72h. After 100 reschedules in that window, new cancels fail. The failure is caught and logged (`console.log('Error canceling reminder...')`), and the email is still sent.

The branch's HEAD commit ("remove immediate delete for request reschedule") moved `requestReschedule` to the deferred path, but `handleNewBooking` was left on the immediate path. `handleNewBooking` is the path for attendee-initiated reschedules, which happen far more often.

Also, with `immediateDelete` the DB row is neither deleted nor marked `cancelled`. If the immediate cancel fails there is nothing to retry it. For step and workflow deletion the row is cascade-deleted immediately afterwards anyway.

### What happens today vs. what will break
This works while the account has fewer than 100 pending cancellations. Once reschedule volume passes that, reschedules again send reminders for the old time slot, which is the bug being fixed.

### Recommendation
Use the deferred path for reschedules, as `requestReschedule` already does:
```ts
deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId);
```
For workflow/step deletion, the rows are cascade-deleted, so the deferred flag can't be kept on them. Either mark them `cancelled` and detach them from the step before deleting it (e.g. make `workflowStepId` nullable / `onDelete: SetNull`), or immediately cancel only reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the cron's 1-hour window.

claim: The DB write that marks reminders cancelled (the only cancellation signal now) is fire-and-forget; the previously awaited reminder deletes were removed from prismaPromises, so a failed or unfinished update is silently lost and the email is sent.
body:
## [ISSUE] The `cancelled: true` write is no longer awaited

**Severity:** LOW — if the write is lost, the reminder is never cancelled and nothing reports it.

### The Problem
```ts
booking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => {
  if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL) {
    deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId);
```
`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is `async`, and its returned promise is dropped. Before this PR, the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` calls were collected into `remindersToDelete` and awaited through `Promise.all(prismaPromises)`. Now the only record that a reminder must be cancelled is the `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` inside that dropped promise. The same pattern appears in `bookings.tsx:490` and `workflows.tsx:378/576`.

### Theory / Proof
- Any error inside it (DB timeout, connection pool exhausted) is swallowed by the helper's `catch` and only goes to `console.log`. The request still returns 200, and the cron never sees the reminder as cancelled.
- In serverless deployments (Vercel), work that is still pending after the handler's promise resolves may be frozen or dropped. The later awaits (`Promise.all(...apiDeletes)`, `sendCancelledEmails`) usually give the writes enough time, but nothing guarantees it.

### Recommendation
Await the cancellations together with the other promises:
```ts
const reminderCancellations = updatedBookings.flatMap((booking) =>
  booking.workflowReminders.map((reminder) =>
    reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL
      ? deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)
      : reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.SMS
      ? deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)
      : Promise.resolve()
  )
);
await Promise.all([attendeeDeletes, bookingReferenceDeletes, ...apiDeletes, ...reminderCancellations]);
```
